record.context_brief: Polynomial numerical indices of classical spaces
record.original_question: Compute the polynomial numerical indices of complex Hilbert spaces and of ℓ_1.

evidence.quote: Problem 36. Compute the polynomial numerical indices of complex Hilbert spaces and of ℓ1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a complex Banach space. For a positive integer $k$, a continuous $k$-homogeneous polynomial from $X$ to $X$ is a map $P:X\to X$ of the form $P(x)=T(x,\dots,x)$ for some continuous symmetric $k$-linear map $T:X^k\to X$. Denote by $\mathcal{P}(^kX;X)$ the Banach space of such polynomials endowed with the norm $\|P\|=\sup\{\|P(x)\|:\|x\|\le 1\}$. The numerical radius of $P\in\mathcal{P}(^kX;X)$ is
$$v(P)=\sup\bigl\{|x^*(P(x))|:x\in X,\ x^*\in X^*,\ \|x\|=\|x^*\|=x^*(x)=1\bigr\}.$$
The polynomial numerical index of order $k$ of $X$ is
$$n^{(k)}(X)=\inf\{v(P):P\in\mathcal{P}(^kX;X),\ \|P\|=1\}.$$
Compute explicitly the values $n^{(k)}(H)$ for every $k\ge 2$, where $H$ is an infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, and the values $n^{(k)}(\ell_1)$ for every $k\ge 2$, where $\ell_1$ is the complex Banach space of absolutely summable sequences.
artifact.category_tag: Polynomial numerical index of Banach spaces
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of computing the polynomial numerical indices $n^{(k)}$ for complex Hilbert spaces and for $\ell_1$ is a well-known open question in the area of numerical indices. Searches reveal partial results in related directions (e.g., polynomial numerical indices of $C(K,X)$ and $L_\infty(\mu,X)$ spaces, and some specific values in the real case), but no source confirms an explicit formula for $n^{(k)}(H)$ on complex Hilbert spaces or for $n^{(k)}(\ell_1)$ for all $k\ge 2$. The current status appears to remain open or only partially understood.

status_evidence.title: The polynomial numerical index for some complex vector-valued function spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Studies polynomial numerical indices of complex vector-valued function spaces such as C(K,X) and L_infty(mu,X), reducing them to those of the range space X.
status_evidence.claim: Related partial results exist but do not compute n^{(k)} of complex Hilbert spaces or ell_1 directly.
